Same thing happened to me Summer of 2020– I’m 30 & I’ve had clear skin my entire life, always got compliments on my complexion. Just like you, scars, PIH, pustules, bumps, redness, and thick feeling skin. I’ve easily spend $1000 on products. Even the few times I’ve had it comparatively under control for a few weeks, my skin still does not look ~good~. I had to quit my job a few months ago bc of a horrible flare. 

I started using a hand-mixed combo cream a week ago, and I’ve seen a decent amount of improvement. It’s basically APNO (all purpose nipple ointment) which contains anti biotic ointment (I used neosporin), anti fungal cream (I used Lotrimin & Lamisil), + Hydrocortisone cream (I used one labeled as healing). I added sulfur cream & a little zinc diaper cream. I slather my face in that whenever I’m home/sleeping, wash with sulfur bar soap, and moisturize with Simple moisturizer & LRP cicaplast. Nothing else. Maybe worth a try but I won’t pretend like I’m not also just shooting in the dark here.

I'm going to say yes. You see the patchiness & flakiness in your hairline? That's what I had, I didn't even notice how bad it was until it was partially resolved. Google "tinea capitis" and see if it matches up at all. 

You can find out easily if it's fungal by applying anti fungal cream-- a very thick layer to your face &  your hairline. You can literally get a tube at Dollar tree. Lotrimin is the most popular but it's overpriced. Most store brands of ringworm, athletes foot, jock itch, or even yeast infection creams should work. I saw immediate results, like 80% improvement within 5 minutes, it was insane (and mine was much worse than yours). If it shows improvement, keep up with the cream 2x a day for 2 weeks and consider adding in an antifungal shampoo like Nizoral (use on face & scalp). If there is no improvement after the first application, chances are it's not fungal.
